task: FLEET MEMBER 3: cross-cutting adversarial + edge-case + dark-pattern testing of the 4a (Foray) search/playlist pipeline

findings.title: 100k-char query crashes interpretQuery with an uncaught 'Invalid regular expression: too large' exception
findings.repro: node _redteam_probe.js (repo root) — query `"b".repeat(100000)`. Also isolated: a query of ~50,000 repeated identical chars triggers it (30,000 chars is fine, 50,000 throws). The UI's `#pl-input`/`#sh-input` both carry `maxlength="120"` (app.js lines 1977, 1982, 2372) so this is NOT reachable through the normal text box — but it IS reachable via any programmatic caller of `SearchEngine.interpretQuery` (devtools console, a future API/import-data path, or a differently-validated caller) since search-engine.js itself enforces no length cap on its own public API. `buildPlaylist()` in app.js has no try/catch around `SearchEngine.interpretQuery(query, ctx)` (app.js line 1496), so if this were ever reached with an uncapped string the exception is unhandled and blanks the app/breaks the submit flow with no user-facing message.
findings.evidence: [CRASH] 100k char string: Invalid regular expression: /(?<![a-z0-9])bbbb...(repeated ~50000 b's)...(?:s|es|ing)?(?![a-z0-9])/: Regular expression too large — from `node _redteam_probe.js`. Root cause: search-engine.js `longTermPattern()` (line ~777-779) builds `new RegExp("(?<![a-z0-9])" + t + ...)` directly from the raw token `t` with no length ceiling before compiling.

findings.title: Cold single-word playlist queries take 1.5-8 seconds end-to-end on a fresh session — no perf ceiling, no loading-state guard visible in app.js, and the search-quality test battery has zero timing assertions
findings.repro: node script (workspace root /workspace/projects/foray/_rt_realistic_first_query.mjs, run 3x): first `interpretQuery`+`searchWithRelaxation` call of a brand-new `ctx` (i.e. what a user's FIRST playlist build in a session actually looks like — `searchCtx()` in app.js builds and caches exactly one such ctx per session at line 790-795) for `"philosophy of science"` took 6.6s, 7.9s, 8.1s across three separate runs; a second, topically-unrelated query in the same warm-ish ctx still took 1.3-3.8s. Root cause: `tagDF`/`corpusDF`/`tagCount` in search-engine.js are O(catalog-size) linear scans per NOVEL term (not per query), memoized only after first use, and a single query token can expand via concept vocabulary into 75+ distinct terms (measured: `interpretQuery('philosophy')` on a fresh ctx touches 76 previously-unmemoized tagDF terms). `tools/test-search.mjs`'s 123-case battery calls `freshCtx()` per test (line 145-147/161) so it exercises this exact cold path on every single case, yet the file has zero timing/latency assertions (grep for Date.now/performance.now/elapsed/latency/timeout returns 1 hit, unrelated to perf).
findings.evidence: node _rt_realistic_first_query.mjs (run 3x): 'FIRST query of a session, "philosophy of science": interpret=3890ms search=4006ms total=7896ms' / 'interpret=3503ms search=3088ms total=6591ms' / 'interpret=4410ms search=3686ms total=8096ms'. Term-expansion measurement: 'interpretQuery("philosophy") on FRESH ctx: 1607 ms / new tagDF-memoized terms: 76'. No blocking-state markers (spinner/disabled-button) were found around the `#pl-form` submit handler in app.js (lines 2021-2040) — the submit is synchronous and the UI has no visible affordance for an 8-second stall.

findings.title: search-engine.js purity claim (pure, no DOM/localStorage/network/LLM at query time) holds — verified
findings.repro: search_files for `async |await |fetch\(|Promise|setTimeout|XMLHttpRequest|localStorage|document\.|window\.` in search-engine.js. Two hits, both benign: a comment on line 2-4 restating the pure-function contract, and the module-export shim at lines 1340-1344 (`if (module.exports) ... else window.SearchEngine = ...`), which only runs at load time, never at query time.
findings.evidence: grep result: only lines 1, 1341, 1343 (comment + export-shim `window.SearchEngine = SearchEngine`) match network/DOM/timer keywords; no `fetch`, `async`, `await`, `Promise`, `setTimeout`, or `localStorage` calls exist anywhere in `interpretQuery`/`scoreMatch`/`searchWithRelaxation`/`classifyResults`/`diversify`.

findings.title: XSS/injection: all dynamic search-result and playlist-query text goes through esc() before innerHTML — no bypass found
findings.repro:
Traced every `results.innerHTML =`/`$("#view").innerHTML =` write that embeds user-controlled text: showResultRow (app.js:1819-1824, `${esc(show.title)}`, `esc(safeUrl(show.artwork_url))`), epRow (app.js:2054-2066, `${esc(item.title)}`), renderPlaylistDetail's `

${esc(p.title)}

` (app.js:2168), renderShowSearchResults' no-match note (line 1920, `No shows match "${query}"...` — but this is set via `.textContent`, not innerHTML, so it needs no escaping and cannot inject HTML), and the pl-note "Not much on... instead" message (app.js:2036-2037) — also `.textContent`, not innerHTML. `playlistPart()`/`prettyTitle()` never emit the raw search string into a playlist's saved `title`/`items` — `prettyTitle()` (app.js:816-825) strips the query to `[a-z0-9]+`-split words before capitalizing, so no HTML-carrying characters ever reach a playlist's stored title in the first place. Probe confirmed `` and `` queries tokenize into inert word fragments (`script`, `alert`) that never survive as literal markup.
findings.evidence: node _redteam_probe.js output: `[OK] script tag: ... tokens containing suspicious chars: ["script","alert","script"]` — these are plain lowercase tokenizer output (matched against catalog text, not re-embedded as markup), and resultCount=0 confirms no catalog item happened to match, so nothing rendered from this query at all in the actual UI path.

findings.title: Show-search race condition (typed-ahead network response) is correctly guarded with a request-token; topic/playlist search has no equivalent risk because it is synchronous
findings.repro: renderShowSearchResults (app.js:1907-1934) uses a module-level counter `showSearchToken`; each call captures `myToken = ++showSearchToken` and both the local-paint callback and the `fetchApiJson(...).then(...)` breadth-search callback check `if (myToken !== showSearchToken) return;` before touching the DOM (lines 1916, 1932) — this correctly prevents a slow in-flight breadth-search fetch from a stale query clobbering a newer query's results. The topic/playlist-builder path (`buildPlaylist`, app.js:1494-1527, wired at the `#pl-form` submit handlers lines 2021-2040 and 2387-2404) has NO async operation at all — `interpretQuery`/`searchWithRelaxation`/`classifyResults` are synchronous pure functions and the result immediately either navigates via `location.hash = ...` or renders `#pl-note` textContent in the same tick — so there is no window for a second, faster query to land first and be overwritten by a slower first query's stale result. This is not a missing-guard bug; it's a correct design (no race is possible because the operation is not concurrent).
findings.evidence: grep confirms `showSearchToken` guard exists (2 checks, lines 1916 & 1932) and buildPlaylist's own call chain contains zero `await`/`.then`/`fetch` (search-engine.js has none of those tokens at all, confirmed above).

findings.title: Dark-pattern check against CLAUDE.md product principle #1 ('no engagement dark patterns... no streaks, no infinite scroll, no autoplay chains'): ranking/classification code is honest — no padding, no hidden sparse status, no artificial inflation found
findings.repro: 1) Read classifyResults (search-engine.js:1186-1260): status is set to "sparse" whenever `strong.length < RICH_MIN`, and the code explicitly documents and enforces (with inline comments citing #216 review findings) that a sparse result is NEVER widened past its genuine strong-match count to fake a fuller list — `widen` only ever narrows toward `strong`/`prefix`, never pads with sub-bar filler. 2) Empirically verified with 25 real concept-term queries against the live catalog: sparse results returned 4-5 picks despite 33-76 total scored candidates being available to pad from (e.g. q="tokamak": status=sparse picks=4 totalCandidates=33 — 29 lower-scoring candidates existed and were correctly withheld, not appended). 3) diversify() (search-engine.js:1150-1184) only ever reorders/spreads an already-adequate candidate set or backfills genuinely-available items in rank order — its own header comment explicitly rejects "capping bbq's 4 same-show episodes down to 2 and calling it sparse" as dishonest and the code doesn't do that (single-show sets keep their un-capped strong list). 4) `sparse: status === "sparse"` is stored plainly on the saved playlist object (app.js:1515) and surfaced to the user verbatim in renderPlaylistDetail ("Only found a few on this — here's what we've got", app.js:2172) — never hidden or relabeled as a full/confident result. No streaks, infinite scroll, or autoplay-chain mechanics exist anywhere in the search/playlist ranking code path (search-engine.js has no session-length, engagement, or time-on-app signal in scoreMatch/classifyResults/diversify at all — scoring inputs are purely text-match strength, tag/topic overlap, and listened-history down-weighting).
findings.evidence: node _rt_sparse_honesty_small.mjs output: 25 real semantic-index concept-term queries, e.g. `q="tokamak" status=sparse picks=4 totalCandidates=33`, `q="plasma" status=sparse picks=4 totalCandidates=33`, `q="ignition" status=sparse picks=5 totalCandidates=33` — picks consistently stay well below DEFAULT_CAP(10) and below totalCandidates despite ample lower-ranked filler being available, confirming the code's documented no-padding rule holds in practice, not just in comments.

areas_clean: search-engine.js purity: no DOM/localStorage/network/LLM calls at query time (only benign module-export shim references `window`)

XSS/HTML-injection: every dynamic innerHTML write of user- or catalog-derived text passes through esc(); textContent assignments (which need no escaping) are used for the two places raw query text is echoed back verbatim (show-search 'no match' note, playlist-builder 'not much on X' note); playlist titles are derived via prettyTitle() which strips to [a-z0-9]+ words before ever being stored/rendered, so no HTML-carrying query ever reaches persisted state

Race conditions: show search has an explicit, correct request-token guard (showSearchToken) against a stale async breadth-search response clobbering a newer query's UI; the playlist/topic-search path is fully synchronous end-to-end so no analogous race is possible there by construction

SQL-injection-shaped, emoji-only, non-English (Chinese/Arabic), null-byte, RTL-override, template-literal, and prototype-pollution-shaped strings: all handled safely — either tokenize to zero content tokens (correctly short-circuiting buildPlaylist to status:'empty' before any scoring runs, confirmed via direct interpretQuery inspection) or tokenize to inert lowercase word fragments matched only against real catalog text, never executed/interpolated as code or re-rendered as unescaped markup

Dark patterns / product principle #1 ('no engagement dark patterns'): ranking code has no engagement/session-length/streak signal at all; sparse results are never padded toward DEFAULT_CAP with lower-quality filler (verified empirically across 25 real queries); the 'sparse' status is stored and surfaced honestly to the user, never hidden or upgraded to look like a confident full result; no autoplay-chain or infinite-scroll mechanics exist in the search/playlist pipeline
